context.title: Questions in the Temple
context.summary: Jesus tells a parable of tenants who kill the owner's son. He answers questions about taxes, the resurrection and the greatest commandment, asks about David's son, warns against showy scribes, and praises a poor widow's gift.
context.background: Leaders of different groups take turns testing Jesus in the temple courts. The Sadducees, a priestly party, denied the resurrection. One scribe, unusually, agrees with Jesus and is told he is 'not far from the kingdom of God' (v. 34).

customs.note: The smallest coins in circulation. Mark explains for Roman readers that two of them equal a quadrans ('farthing'), a tiny Roman coin.
If a man died childless, his brother married the widow to carry on the family line (Deuteronomy 25:5-6).

watchFor: The Shema, 'Hear, O Israel', opens Jesus' answer about the first commandment (v. 29).
Scribes who 'devour widows' houses' (v. 40) set up the widow's story that follows.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

events.title: Debates in the Temple
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:23 – Luke 21:4. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.
